targets.hook: Bengals' clear TE1/slot weapon: 7 targets, 78 yds, TD Wk1
targets.why: Gesicki led Cincinnati in catches, targets and receiving yards in Week 1 (5/7 for 78 yards and a TD), working as a de facto slot receiver behind Chase and Higgins drawing coverage. TE is the shallowest skill position in this format by design (only 12 startable TE slots across the league, no TE-premium scoring), so a clear No.-1-target tight end on the wire is a real market inefficiency (CBS Sports, 2026-09-14).
targets.asset: 5 rec / 7 tgt / 78 yds / 1 TD in Week 1, TE4 in points scored through Sunday
targets.rate_basis: recent-trend (wk 1, first data point of the season)
targets.my_team_impact: My TE2 is Juwan Johnson, a mid-tier Saints option behind starter Isaiah Likely. Gesicki's clean No.-1-target role is a direct upgrade for bye/injury insurance and standalone flex value.
targets.confidence_why: One-game sample, but the role (leading the team in every receiving category with Chase/Higgins drawing coverage) is structural, not a fluke.
targets.competition: No dossiers exist yet for this first-season league; no rival roster shows a specific TE hole beyond the ordinary shallow-TE churn.
targets.bid: unpriced -- year one, no bidding history in this league yet. 12 teams on 100 FAAB chase a thinner pool than the HBGBs' 10, so HBGBs prices would read low here.
targets.drop: Juwan Johnson is a real bench TE but without Gesicki's clear target funnel; a plausible scoop for another single-TE roster if dropped.
